verdict.rationale: MoQ ships non-GUI components of its own that suit unattended automation: the moq-cli tool imports and publishes broadcasts (including via ffmpeg), and moq-relay is a standalone server. A production report also describes programmatic headless subscribers (an S3 archiver and a transcription service) running against a relay. Nothing documents CI usage, a headless mode or non-interactive automation guidance, so only part of the story is evidenced. missing for 10: explicit CI/headless documentation, documented non-interactive flags or config for scripted runs, container or CI pipeline examples, independent corroboration of use in CI.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can run the product headlessly / in CI for automation

citations.quote: A CLI that can import and publish MoQ broadcasts from a variety of formats (fMP4, HLS, MPEG-TS, FLV, etc), including via ffmpeg.
A server connecting publishers to subscribers, able to form a [self-hosted CDN cluster]
Or run on native with polyfills via Node/Bun/Deno.
publish Opus to one relay, which fans out to independent subscribers: an S3 archiver, Zoom Scribe Live transcription, and voice ID
